title: Peace! the Welcome Sound Proclaim
description: Peace! the Welcome Sound Proclaim in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 812 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Blessings of Peace”, where the book credits them to the Lewins Mead Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Peace! the wel-come sound pro-claim, Dwell with rap-ture on the theme; Loud, still loud-er, swell the strain: Peace on earth, good will to men.

lines: Dwell with rapture on the theme;
Loud, still louder, swell the strain:
Peace on earth, good will to men.
Peace on earth, good will to men.
Loud still louder, swell the strain,
Peace on earth, good will to men.
Loud, still louder, swell the strain,
Praise to God, good will to men.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
